materiality: MultiModalHasher previously hashed an unframed byte stream in which distinct caller-controlled mm_processor_kwargs shapes could collide across key/value boundaries, nested-versus-dotted keys, sequence-versus-mapping shapes, None-versus-empty values and empty-versus-omitted containers.

The resulting mm_hash identifies the multimodal processor cache and is also included in prefix-cache block hashing, so a collision can silently associate a request with processed multimodal features or KV blocks derived from a different request.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact vLLM source/image, model/tokenizer/processor revisions, hash algorithm, media-byte hashes, mm_processor_kwargs canonical input and prefix-cache configuration.

Run the upstream predecessor against all documented collision pairs and preserve exact equal-digest evidence; prove the candidate produces distinct digests for each pair while preserving deterministic same-input identity.

Exercise processor-cache and prefix-cache hits/misses, nested/flat mappings, lists/maps, None/empty/omitted values, multiple modalities, concurrent tenants/requests and restart boundaries; prove no cache entry created for one request is returned for a distinct framed input.
Measure preprocessing overhead only after cache-isolation correctness; retain cache-disable as rollback and do not infer cryptographic collision resistance beyond the framed serialization contract.

materiality: Aria expert checkpoints could not load because name conversion left an extra .weight suffix and HF/vLLM expert tensors use different layouts; correcting only the name still produced shape failures.
The successor fixes Aria-specific mapping and transpose behavior while preserving quantization mapper names; upstream CPU parity passed but full-model GPU qualification was not run.
requiredEvidence: Resolve and bind the exact Aria checkpoint/config/tokenizer/processor revision and file identities together with exact vLLM/Transformers/Torch runtime and quantization configuration.

Run the immediate predecessor as a known-bad load control and preserve missing-name/shape-failure evidence; prove the candidate consumes every expected expert/shared-expert tensor exactly once with expected post-transform shapes and no unexpected leftovers.

Compare deterministic HF-reference and vLLM MoE outputs/logits across FP32/BF16, top-k 1/2, multiple token counts and applicable quantized paths; require full-model accelerator inference before any serving qualification.

Exercise save/load/startup failure, partial or malformed checkpoint controls, quantization mapper names and rollback to the previously qualified Aria path; no model artifact is mirrored for inventory.

materiality: This is an additive successor to the already governed SafeUnpickler exact-allowlist boundary: module-prefix trust still admitted callable helpers, and torch.storage._load_from_bytes invoked a nested deserializer outside the outer allowlist.
The successor replaces remaining code-module prefixes with exact module/name entries and routes nested storage bytes through torch.load(weights_only=True) with storage-result validation.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang/Python/Torch source and the serialization/weight-cache protocol version; record the previously governed SafeUnpickler revision separately and do not inherit its qualification.

Construct deterministic malicious/negative payloads covering rejected callable globals, nested torch.storage bytes, unexpected object types and disallowed reconstruction helpers; prove the predecessor admits the targeted boundary where reproducible and the candidate rejects it fail-closed.

Run legitimate tensor/storage/encoder metadata/weight-cache protocol round-trips including nested storage on CPU and supported accelerator/server paths; missing accelerator coverage remains UNQUALIFIED, not PASS.
Preserve weights_only nested loading, exact allowlists, no remote-code execution, rollback and existing artifact/provenance checks; never weaken deserialization policy to preserve compatibility.

materiality: GLM-OCR with EAGLE/MTP on image inputs could hit CUDA out-of-bounds memory access when the draft model attempted to look up image placeholder IDs in the vocabulary rather than reuse target-model multimodal embeddings.
The successor also carries MRoPE positions through speculative steps and into draft CUDA-graph buffers, making embedding ownership and positional state part of the verification contract.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang source/image, GLM-OCR target/draft checkpoint and processor revisions, MTP/EAGLE settings, multimodal input hashes, CUDA/Torch stack and CUDA-graph mode.

Run the predecessor known-bad image/MTP path under memory checking where feasible and preserve the CUDA OOB or equivalent failure; prove candidate target embeddings are reused without vocabulary lookup of image placeholders.

Compare greedy outputs against a non-MTP baseline with CUDA graphs enabled and disabled, single and concurrent requests, multiple image sizes/counts and repeated speculative steps; record MRoPE positions and prove monotonic/correct advancement into graph replay buffers.
Exercise cancellation/restart, graph recapture, text-only controls and malformed multimodal inputs; require no OOB/NaN and preserve non-MTP as rollback before throughput claims.

materiality: SGLang process placement/rank reads previously depended on process-group state and a parallel runner record, allowing runtime context and frozen records to disagree, including pipeline swaps and several speculative draft-worker scopes.

The successor records launcher-known placement at publish time, derives attention ranks through one arithmetic path and explicitly refuses to record moe_dp_rank in the topology where launcher and group semantics differ.
requiredEvidence: Bind exact SGLang source/image, launcher mode, TP/PP/DP/CP/EP widths and rank bundle, speculative mode, scheduler entrypoint, distributed backend and accelerator topology.

Cross-check published ranks against process-group-derived ranks over a topology matrix including tp2, tp2+pp2, dp attention and missing/None rank fields; assert the explicit moe_dp_rank fallthrough case instead of coercing conflicting semantics.

Exercise pipeline-group swaps, all six speculative worker construction/backend-init/graph-capture scopes and state retained after scope exit; prove target/draft context cannot leak topology across workers or lifecycle transitions.

PP plus speculative decoding remains UNQUALIFIED unless an executable supported checkpoint/path produces independent runtime evidence; upstream unit coverage or non-spec token parity must not close that gate.
